findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:484 — Booking cancellation no longer cancels scheduled emails immediately: deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called without immediateDelete, so it only sets cancelled: true and defers the real SendGrid cancellation to the scheduleEmailReminders cron; any reminder firing before the next cron run is still delivered for a cancelled booking, making the cancel path inconsistent with the reschedule path (handleNewBooking.ts:968 uses immediateDelete=true) and regressing vs. the old immediate cancel

[Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:50-72 — The cancel loop awaits SendGrid sequentially inside one try/catch and only issues prisma deletes after the entire loop; a single failing request aborts the loop, skips all remaining cancellations, and since PrismaPromises are lazy the already-pushed deletes never execute; the error is only console.log'd, so one poison reminder blocks cancellation of all others on every cron run

[Medium/concurrency] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 (also handleCancelBooking.ts:484, bookings.tsx:484, workflows.tsx) — All reminder cancellations are fire-and-forget (unawaited forEach), a regression from the previously awaited prisma deletes; on serverless the lambda can freeze right after the response, so neither the SendGrid/Twilio calls nor the cancelled-flag update the cron depends on may ever run

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The old booking's reminders are cancelled/deleted at the very start of the reschedule branch, before eventManager.reschedule and the new booking are confirmed; if any later step throws, the original booking remains active but has no reminders left

[Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:229 — Cancellation failures are swallowed with console.log inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder; callers cannot detect failure and there is no retry, so a failed prisma update or failed SendGrid cancel leaves the reminder active and it will still be sent, silently

[Medium/test_gap] PR-wide — No tests cover any of the new semantics: the soft-cancel flag flow, the cron's cancel-and-delete block, immediateDelete vs. deferred paths, or reminder cleanup on cancel/reschedule/workflow-edit; all critical notification paths were rewritten with zero coverage

[Low/data] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:208 — The immediateDelete branch cancels in SendGrid but performs no DB write, so in the handleNewBooking reschedule path the old booking's WorkflowReminder rows (scheduled=true, cancelled=null) are orphaned forever with no cron query ever matching them; the parameter name is also misleading since nothing is deleted

[Low/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:178 — The prisma delete now sits after await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId) inside the same try block; if Twilio throws (e.g., the message already went out), the DB row is never removed, whereas the old code deleted the row independently of the cancel result

[Low/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/components/WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 — Condition narrowed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded, dropping the sendTo/verification block whenever only isSenderIdNeeded is true; if sender-ID steps relied on this input UI it is now unreachable and isSenderIdNeeded may now be unused — should be confirmed as intentional or split out of this PR

[Low/test_gap] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:78 — The new design depends on the unscheduled-reminders query excluding cancelled: true rows; if it doesn't, a cancelled reminder whose SendGrid cancel failed will be picked up by the scheduling query on a later run and sent anyway — verify the filter exists and add a regression test

[Low/performance] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43 — findMany on WorkflowReminder filtered only by cancelled: true + date, with no index on cancelled/scheduledDate, no pagination/limit, and full-row selects; this table grows with every booking×reminder and the query runs on every cron invocation

[Low/doc_defect] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:901-960 — Roughly 60 lines (the commented team-plan block and the example-booking query) had their indentation stripped to column 0; functionally harmless but an accidental formatting regression that will fight prettier and pollute future diffs

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:484 — Booking cancellation no longer cancels scheduled emails immediately: deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called without immediateDelete, so it only sets cancelled: true and defers the real SendGrid cancellation to the scheduleEmailReminders cron; any reminder firing before the next cron run is still delivered for a cancelled booking, making the cancel path inconsistent with the reschedule path (handleNewBooking.ts:968 uses immediateDelete=true) and regressing vs. the old immediate cancel

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the cancel path now calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) without immediateDelete. Per emailReminderManager.ts, when referenceId exists and immediateDelete is falsy, it does NOT cancel the SendGrid scheduled send; it only marks the WorkflowReminder row as cancelled=true. Actual SendGrid cancellation is deferred to scheduleEmailReminders.ts, which later finds cancelled reminders (within the next hour) and cancels/deletes them. This is a behavior regression vs the previous immediate cancellation (old code called deleteScheduledEmailReminder(referenceId) and then deleted DB rows) and is inconsistent with the reschedule path in handleNewBooking.ts which calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true) for immediate cancellation. Therefore a cancelled booking can still have a SendGrid scheduled email pending until the cron/API job runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:50-72 — The cancel loop awaits SendGrid sequentially inside one try/catch and only issues prisma deletes after the entire loop; a single failing request aborts the loop, skips all remaining cancellations, and since PrismaPromises are lazy the already-pushed deletes never execute; the error is only console.log'd, so one poison reminder blocks cancellation of all others on every cron run

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block does `await client.request(...)` inside a `for...of` loop, then only *collects* `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls into `workflowRemindersToDelete` and runs them at the end via `await Promise.all(...)`. If any `client.request` throws, control jumps to the `catch` and `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached, so none of the already-collected Prisma deletes execute (Prisma queries are lazy until awaited). This means one failing SendGrid cancellation can prevent deletion of all reminders processed so far and all remaining reminders, causing repeated retries on subsequent runs, with only a `console.log` for visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The old booking's reminders are cancelled/deleted at the very start of the reschedule branch, before eventManager.reschedule and the new booking are confirmed; if any later step throws, the original booking remains active but has no reminders left

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts` the new code cancels/deletes `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` immediately upon entering the `if (originalRescheduledBooking?.uid)` branch (calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)`) before the subsequent `await eventManager.reschedule(...)` runs. Since `eventManager.reschedule` is not wrapped in a transaction or catch here, if it throws, the original booking can remain in its prior state while its reminders have already been cancelled and (for SMS, also deleted from DB in `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`), leaving an inconsistent/broken state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:229 — Cancellation failures are swallowed with console.log inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder; callers cannot detect failure and there is no retry, so a failed prisma update or failed SendGrid cancel leaves the reminder active and it will still be sent, silently

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, both `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` wrap all cancellation/DB operations in `try/catch` and only `console.log` on error without rethrowing (`emailReminderManager.ts` and `smsReminderManager.ts`). Call sites shown in the diff commonly invoke these functions inside `forEach` without `await` (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, `workflows.tsx`), so failures are neither awaited nor propagated. If the SendGrid/Twilio cancel or the Prisma `update/delete` fails, the reminder may remain scheduled/uncancelled and can still be sent, with the rest of the cancellation/reschedule flow proceeding as if it succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new reminder-cancellation semantics (e.g., new `cancelled` column and soft-cancel flow in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, new cancel-and-delete block in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, and rewritten cancel/reschedule/workflow-edit cleanup paths calling the new signatures). The PR diff does not add or modify any test files to exercise these new branches (immediateDelete vs deferred, cancelled-flag processing, reschedule/cancel cleanup), so it’s a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a functional defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:178 — The prisma delete now sits after await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId) inside the same try block; if Twilio throws (e.g., the message already went out), the DB row is never removed, whereas the old code deleted the row independently of the cancel result

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder now does `if (referenceId) await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId);` and then deletes the DB row in the same `try` block. If `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` throws, execution jumps to `catch` and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` never runs. In this diff, the previous callers’ independent Prisma deletions (e.g., the removed `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` loops in handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings router, workflows router) are gone, so a Twilio cancel failure can now leave the WorkflowReminder row undeleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/ee/workflows/components/WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 — Condition narrowed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded, dropping the sendTo/verification block whenever only isSenderIdNeeded is true; if sender-ID steps relied on this input UI it is now unreachable and isSenderIdNeeded may now be unused — should be confirmed as intentional or split out of this PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `WorkflowStepContainer.tsx` changes the render guard from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to only `isPhoneNumberNeeded`, which definitively removes the entire sendTo/verification UI when `isSenderIdNeeded` is true but `isPhoneNumberNeeded` is false. The diff does not show any alternative UI for the sender-id-only case, and it also suggests `isSenderIdNeeded` may now be unused. Whether this is an actual functional bug depends on whether sender-id-only steps exist/are reachable, which cannot be confirmed from the diff alone, but it is a concrete regression risk introduced by this change and should be confirmed as intentional or refactored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:78 — The new design depends on the unscheduled-reminders query excluding cancelled: true rows; if it doesn't, a cancelled reminder whose SendGrid cancel failed will be picked up by the scheduling query on a later run and sent anyway — verify the filter exists and add a regression test

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cancelled` flag and changes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to *not* delete the DB row for scheduled email reminders (it `update`s `cancelled: true` unless `immediateDelete`), relying on `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` to later cancel/delete those rows. That creates a real edge-case to verify: the later “unscheduled Email reminders” `findMany` must not pick up `cancelled: true` rows, or they could be re-scheduled if they ever qualify as “unscheduled”. However, the diff excerpt does not show the full `unscheduledReminders` query, so we can’t confirm whether the filter exists; the request to verify and add a regression test is still a specific, diff-grounded review point rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43 — findMany on WorkflowReminder filtered only by cancelled: true + date, with no index on cancelled/scheduledDate, no pagination/limit, and full-row selects; this table grows with every booking×reminder and the query runs on every cron invocation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new cron-time query in `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that does `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})` with no `take`/pagination and no `select`, so it will load all matching rows (full row payload) each run. The migration/schema only add a nullable `cancelled` column and do not add any index (no `@@index([cancelled, scheduledDate])` or SQL index shown), so as the `WorkflowReminder` table grows this can become a real performance/scalability concern introduced by this change. This is a review-worthy issue but not a correctness defect by itself.
